h: Gardens, Castles and Wading Birds Close By
p: A compact zoo like this is a perfect half-day, which leaves you the other half to explore one of the most underrated corners of Cumbria. South Lakeland sits where the fells meet Morecambe Bay, and it's full of surprises that many people speed past on the M6.

Garden lovers should head to Levens Hall, a few miles north of Milnthorpe, where the topiary garden is full of clipped yews in wonderful, slightly bonkers shapes. Nearby, Sizergh, run by the National Trust, has a medieval tower at its heart, plus gardens, a rock garden and estate walks. Both are lovely on a dry day and easy to pair with a morning among the snow leopards. Kendal, a little further on, is a handsome market town and the home of Kendal Mint Cake, the energy snack that has gone up mountains around the world.

For something wilder, RSPB Leighton Moss near Silverdale is a big reedbed reserve where you might spot marsh harriers or hear bitterns booming in spring, and the hides make it a fun hunt for young naturalists. Arnside, on the Kent estuary, has a promenade with views across the sands and the railway viaduct striding across the water. Keep an ear out for the tidal bore and the siren warning of incoming tides, and never wander out onto the sands. They're beautiful but treacherous.
Back at the zoo, the evolution route works best if you follow it in order, so take the time to go round as it's laid out. It's a neat way to help kids understand how all those animals fit together.
